title: feat: agent run tokens keep the key's account permissions
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Agent run tokens (`ag_`) now carry the parent key's account permissions (`profile`, `usage`, `keys`, `machines`) along with its model list. Until now, everything except models was stripped.
- The owner decides what an agent may do through the key they call it with. Run tokens no longer have a rule of their own, so a `/grant?permission=machines` link from an agent's 403 now works.
- Endpoint agents receive the token on their own server. `AGENTS_AND_MCP.md` now says to call third-party agents with a key that holds only what they need. Keys created in the dashboard start with no account permissions.
- Fixes the stale line in `account.md` that said child keys can't get `account:keys`. They can since #15450.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Parent key has `machines` | Run token gets 403 | Run token can run sandboxes |
| Parent key has no account permissions | No account access | No account access |

Follows up on the discussion in #16407.

gist.headline: The agent gets its keys
gist.blurb: An agent sent to tend a sandbox can carry the permissions its owner gave it. No more asking the gate twice.
gist.summary: Agent run tokens (`ag_`) inherit the parent key’s `profile`, `usage`, `keys`, and `machines` account permissions alongside its model list, so agents can use authorized account actions without gaining permissions the key lacks.
gist.impact: An agent called with a key that has `machines` permission can run sandboxes through its run token; a key with no account permissions still grants the agent no account access.
